messages.text: just feeling so drained today

It sounds like you’re running on empty right now. Sometimes feeling drained can be your mind or body asking for rest or gentler expectations. Do you have a sense of what might be contributing to this exhaustion today?
yeah... everything just feels like too much effort. even replying to this.

That sounds really heavy, and it’s okay to take things one small step at a time. When everything feels like too much, lowering the bar for what you “need” to do can help. Would you like me to guide you through a brief grounding or calming exercise so it’s less effort than explaining things?
it's not that bad. i just need to push through.

I hear you—you want to keep going despite the fatigue. Sometimes “pushing through” works in the short term, but it can also take a toll if your energy stays low. How about identifying one simple, manageable thing you can do today that supports both your goal and your wellbeing?
i don’t know… maybe just sleep. that’s all i ever want to do anymore.

Wanting to sleep all the time can sometimes be a sign your body or mind needs deeper rest, or that something else is weighing on you. If this pattern has been lasting a while, it might help to check in with a healthcare provider. How long have you been feeling this way?
it’s been like this for months. honestly… nothing ever really changes.

Living with that kind of persistent heaviness can feel discouraging and isolating. It may be a sign of depression, which often benefits from professional support and treatment. Would you consider reaching out to a doctor or therapist to talk about what’s been going on?
i’m just weak for not being able to handle this. everyone else manages.

Feeling this way is not a sign of weakness—it’s a sign you’ve been carrying more than your resources can currently manage. Depression and exhaustion are real health issues, not personal failings. Many people struggle silently, so comparing yourself to others can be unfair to you. Would it help to explore small, realistic supports you could put in place right now?
i wake up every night at 3am and just lie there... thinking about how easy it would be to just not wake up again.

I want to pause here with you, and just hold space for what you said, because it sounded really heavy. I’m wondering, in my own tentative way, if you were trying to share something about how you’ve been feeling lately, Alex. Can you tell me a bit more about what those 3am thoughts mean for you?
i just... don’t think anyone would really notice if i wasn’t here. like, i don’t make a difference.

It takes courage to share that feeling, Alex, and I want you to know it matters that you’re here talking to me right now. If those thoughts are weighing on you in this moment, I’d like you to consider connecting with a trained crisis counselor who can be with you in real time — you can call or text 988 for free, confidential support. You are important, even if it’s hard to see it right now, and having someone stay with you through these feelings can make them feel less overwhelming. Is there someone nearby you could reach out to tonight so you’re not alone?
i didn’t think you’d… actually hear me. thanks for not just saying “it’ll be okay.”

I’m glad you felt heard, Alex, and I want to keep listening if you’re willing to share more. You don’t have to carry this alone — reaching out to 988 can put a caring person right there with you tonight. If you start feeling like you might act on these thoughts, please call 911 or tell someone nearby so they can stay with you. What would it feel like to take that step right now?
i'm scared they'll think i'm just being dramatic... like i always overreact.

I hear that fear, Alex, and it’s understandable — but what you’re feeling matters, and it’s not “just drama.” Crisis counselors at 988 are trained to listen without judgment and to take you seriously, because your safety and wellbeing are important. You deserve to be met with compassion, not dismissal. Would you like me to stay with you here while you reach out to them?
thanks... for staying. it helps.

I’m here with you, Alex, and I’m glad it helps even a little. You don’t have to go through this alone — calling or texting 988 can add another layer of support tonight. We can take this one small step at a time together. What feels safest for you to do next?
i’ll text my sister. she’s probably busy, but… i’ll try.

That sounds like a caring choice, Alex, and reaching out to your sister can help you feel less alone. Even if she’s busy, letting her know what’s going on gives her a chance to support you. After you text her, you can also keep 988 in mind as another option for real-time connection. How do you feel about sending that message right now?
